title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten no-purchase outings for Hofstra students and friends, spanning free campus culture, recreation, and admission-free New York City destinations.

cards.title: Browse the Emily Lowe Gallery
cards.subtitle: Free art viewing on Hofstra’s South Campus
cards.notes: Meet behind Emily Lowe Hall, browse the current exhibition together, and check the visitor page before arriving during recesses or installations.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission gallery meetup centered on original exhibitions from Hofstra’s art collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra states that its Museum of Art is open to the public year-round with free admission; Emily Lowe Gallery is one of its exhibition facilities.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public with free admission. Gallery closures apply during major holidays, university recesses, and exhibition installations.

cards.entity_name: Hofstra University Museum of Art Campus Sculpture Tour
cards.title: Follow the Campus Sculpture Tour
cards.subtitle: A self-guided outdoor art walk across Hofstra
cards.notes: Pick up self-guided material at Emily Lowe Gallery, then walk the campus collection and compare how several outdoor works address public memory.
cards.short_summary: An independent campus walk linking Hofstra’s outdoor sculptures through a shared interpretive theme.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum lists an ongoing, self-guided Campus Sculpture Tour and says museum admission is free.
cards.access_notes: The tour is ongoing and self-guided; materials are provided in Emily Lowe Gallery. Check gallery access before collecting materials.

cards.title: Swim Laps at the Swim Center
cards.subtitle: ID-access pool time for the Hofstra community
cards.notes: Bring a valid Hofstra ID, choose a posted open-swim window, and meet poolside for laps or an easy recreational swim without buying admission.
cards.short_summary: A free campus swim session for eligible Hofstra students, faculty, and staff.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra states that students, faculty, and staff may swim at the Hofstra Swim Center free of charge with a valid Hofstra ID.
cards.access_notes: Limited to Hofstra students, faculty, and staff with valid Hofstra ID. Use the current seasonal hours posted by the Swim Center.

cards.entity_name: Archives in Literature, Scholarly Work and Everyday Life Mini-Symposium
cards.title: Join the Archives Mini-Symposium
cards.subtitle: A free October 2026 cultural program at Hofstra
cards.notes: Register in advance, choose a panel that fits your schedule, and stay afterward to compare notes on how archives shape scholarship and daily life.
cards.short_summary: An extended public discussion connecting archival research, literature, and everyday experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra lists the mini-symposium for October 26, 2026, and states that Cultural Center signature events are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; advance registration is requested. Scheduled for October 26, 2026, from 2:40-8 p.m.

cards.title: Plan a Central Park Hang
cards.subtitle: A free park outing featured in Hofstra’s NYC guide
cards.notes: Pack water and a Frisbee, select one lawn or walking loop as the meetup point, and keep the outing purchase-free by bringing what you need.
cards.short_summary: A flexible group day built around walking, relaxing, or tossing a Frisbee in Central Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra includes relaxing, walking, jogging, and playing Frisbee in Central Park among the free activities in its New York City guide.
cards.source_title: Campus Life: New York City | Hofstra University
cards.access_notes: The park activity requires no admission or purchase. Transportation between Hofstra and New York City is not included and may cost money.

cards.title: See the New Year’s Ball Up Close
cards.subtitle: A free Times Square stop from Hofstra’s city guide
cards.notes: Meet in Times Square, enter the visitor center together, and look for the displayed New Year’s Ball without making shopping part of the plan.
cards.short_summary: A no-purchase Times Square meetup focused on a recognizable piece of New Year’s history.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra’s guide places the Times Square Visitor Center among its free NYC activities and says visitors can see a previous New Year’s Ball there.
cards.source_title: Campus Life: New York City | Hofstra University
cards.access_notes: The featured visit requires no purchase. Confirm the visitor center’s current access before departure; transportation to Manhattan may cost money.

cards.title: Meet on the Bryant Park Lawn
cards.subtitle: A free Midtown pause highlighted by Hofstra
cards.notes: Choose a clear meeting point, bring your own snack or sketchbook, and spend an hour talking or relaxing on the lawn behind the public library.
cards.short_summary: A simple Midtown gathering that uses Bryant Park’s lawn as a shared social space.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra identifies Bryant Park as a place to relax on the grass within its guide to free New York City activities.
cards.source_title: Campus Life: New York City | Hofstra University
cards.access_notes: Relaxing in the park requires no admission or purchase. Seasonal attractions may charge; transportation from Hofstra may also cost money.

cards.title: Walk the High Line Together
cards.subtitle: A free elevated-park route in Hofstra’s NYC guide
cards.notes: Pick one entrance as the meetup point, walk a defined section together, and pause to compare plantings and street views along the elevated route.
cards.short_summary: A social walk combining urban views, public art surroundings, and varied plantings above Manhattan streets.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra features the High Line—an elevated public park with hundreds of plant species—in its guide to free NYC activities.
cards.source_title: Campus Life: New York City | Hofstra University
cards.access_notes: Walking the public park requires no admission or purchase. Check current park access and note that transportation from Hofstra may cost money.

cards.title: Cross the Brooklyn Bridge on Foot
cards.subtitle: A free skyline walk recommended in Hofstra’s guide
cards.notes: Start from one end, stay in the designated pedestrian area, and pause only where safe so the group can take in the skyline without blocking traffic.
cards.short_summary: A landmark walk connecting Manhattan and Brooklyn with open skyline views along the route.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra lists walking the Brooklyn Bridge and using its walking paths among the free activities in its New York City guide.
cards.source_title: Campus Life: New York City | Hofstra University
cards.access_notes: Pedestrian crossing requires no admission or purchase. Use designated paths; transportation between Hofstra and the bridge may cost money.

cards.entity_name: National Museum of the American Indian
cards.title: Explore the National Museum of the American Indian
cards.subtitle: A free-admission museum named in Hofstra’s NYC guide
cards.notes: Choose one gallery as a starting point, explore at an unhurried pace, and regroup afterward to share one object or story each person noticed.
cards.short_summary: A free museum outing centered on Indigenous art, histories, and cultures in Lower Manhattan.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra lists the National Museum of the American Indian under “Free Admission” in its New York City museum guide.
cards.source_title: Campus Life: New York City | Hofstra University
cards.access_notes: Museum admission requires no purchase. Check the museum’s current visitor requirements; transportation from Hofstra may cost money.

warnings: Six New York City activities have no admission or purchase requirement, but transportation from Hofstra is not free and is explicitly excluded from each cost claim.
The Swim Center card is restricted to Hofstra students, faculty, and staff with valid identification.
The Archives Mini-Symposium is date-specific and requires advance registration.
